title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the alternator warning lamp (L-terminal) circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. This line lets the computer and the alternator talk about charging, so a fault here can affect charging.
symptoms: Check engine or battery light on
Battery may run down over time
Dim or flickering lights in some cases

causes.name: Signal wire in the alternator warning lamp (L-terminal) circuit shorted to ground or open
Failed alternator
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the alternator warning lamp (L-terminal) circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the alternator.

title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the alternator warning lamp (L-terminal) circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. This line lets the computer and the alternator talk about charging, so a fault here can affect charging.
symptoms: Check engine or battery light on
Battery may run down over time
Dim or flickering lights in some cases

causes.name: Signal wire shorted to voltage or a broken ground wire
Failed alternator
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the alternator warning lamp (L-terminal) circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the alternator.

title: Charging System Voltage
plain: The computer sees that the charging system voltage is not where it should be. The alternator may not be charging the battery properly.
symptoms: Check engine or battery light on
Battery may go dead
Dim or flickering lights

causes.name: Failing alternator
Loose or worn drive belt
Loose or corroded battery or alternator cables
Blown alternator fuse or fusible link
Wiring fault between alternator and computer

checks: Test battery voltage with the engine off and running (about 12.6 off and 13.5 to 14.7 running)
Check the drive belt and battery cable connections
Have the alternator load tested
fix: Often a new alternator, but clean and tighten the cables and check the belt first.

title: Charging System Voltage Low
plain: The charging system voltage is lower than it should be, so the battery is not being recharged fully while you drive.
symptoms: Battery light or check engine light on
Battery runs down or the car will not start
Dim lights or weak accessories

causes.name: Failing alternator
Slipping or broken drive belt
Corroded or loose battery or alternator cables
Blown charging fuse
Very heavy electrical load from add-on accessories

checks: Measure voltage at the battery with the engine running
Inspect the belt and the alternator and battery connections
Have the battery and alternator tested
fix: Usually an alternator replacement after confirming the belt and cables are good.

title: Charging System Voltage High
plain: The charging system is putting out more voltage than it should. Too much voltage can damage the battery and electronics.
symptoms: Battery or check engine light on
Very bright or flickering lights
Battery may smell or swell from overcharging

causes.name: Faulty voltage regulator inside the alternator
Bad sense or ground wire to the alternator
Battery with an internal fault
Engine computer charging control fault

checks: Measure battery voltage with the engine running (much above 15 volts is too high)
Check alternator and engine ground connections
Test the battery
fix: Usually a new alternator (or regulator), after checking the ground and sense wiring.

title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal
plain: The computer is watching the power supply circuit to the engine computer and has spotted a fault in its circuit. The engine computer needs a steady supply voltage to run everything else correctly.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Hard starting or stalling in some cases
Other electrical codes may appear

causes.name: Weak battery or loose, corroded battery terminals
Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the engine computer power relay
Broken or chafed wire in the power supply circuit to the engine computer
Failed engine computer power relay
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the power supply circuit to the engine computer, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Fix the battery, cable or wiring fault first; replace the power relay or fuse if bad. The engine computer itself is rarely the cause.

title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the power supply circuit to the engine computer and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. The engine computer needs a steady supply voltage to run everything else correctly.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Hard starting or stalling in some cases
Other electrical codes may appear

causes.name: Weak battery or loose, corroded battery terminals
Failing or sticking engine computer power relay
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the power supply circuit to the engine computer reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Fix the battery, cable or wiring fault first; replace the power relay or fuse if bad. The engine computer itself is rarely the cause.

title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the engine oil level sensor and has spotted a fault in its circuit. This sensor tells the car how much oil is in the oil pan.
symptoms: Check engine light or oil level warning on
Oil level reading may be missing or wrong

causes.name: Oil level actually too low or too high
Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the oil level sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the engine oil level sensor circuit
Failed oil level sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer

checks: Check the oil level with the dipstick (if equipped) before driving
Look over the connector and wiring for the engine oil level sensor, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the oil level sensor.

title: Engine Oil Level Too Low
plain: The oil level sensor says the engine is low on oil. Running an engine low on oil can cause serious damage.
symptoms: Oil level warning or check engine light on
Engine may tick or knock if very low
Oil pressure light may come on

causes.name: Oil level actually low from leaks or burning
Overdue oil change
Faulty oil level sensor
Car parked on a steep slope when checked

checks: Park on level ground and check the oil level right away
Look for oil leaks under the car
Top up with the correct oil before driving further
fix: Add oil to the correct level and find out why it was low; replace the sensor only if the level is actually fine.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the engine computer power relay sense circuit and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. The relay that powers the engine computer is not reporting back as expected.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Car may not start or may stall
Engine may stay powered after shut-off

causes.name: Failing or sticking engine computer power relay
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the engine computer power relay sense circuit reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the engine computer power relay itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the event data recorder request circuit and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. This is the line used to tell the crash data recorder to save information. It does not affect how the car drives.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Wiring or connector fault between the modules
Loose or corroded connector
Airbag or crash data module fault
Engine computer fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the event data recorder request circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector between the modules; module replacement is rarely needed.

title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "B" Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor and has spotted a fault in its circuit. This sensor tells the computer how much pressure is in the A/C system so it can protect the compressor.
symptoms: Check engine light on
A/C may blow warm or cut out
Cooling fans may run more than usual

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor

Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor.
